result.summary: Do not ship: remote error text can now inject clickable HTML into notifications.

findings.title: HTML injection enables phishing through remote scan errors
findings.body: After a successful scan, a remote command can fail with output such as `Reconnect your account`. sshcp.py:155 preserves that output in SshcpError; remote_scanner.py:85-88 and scanner_process.py:91-94 propagate it into scan status; header.component.ts:96-108 passes it into this notification without escaping. The changed binding renders the link where interpolation previously displayed literal text. Angular's sanitizer blocks executable markup but permits safe HTML ([documentation](https://angular.dev/best-practices/security)), so it does not preserve the former protection against injected notification content. A compromised remote server can present an actionable phishing link inside the application.
findings.recommendation: Keep notification text interpolated. Represent intentional links as separate validated fields rendered by the template, and test malicious error text against the actual component template rather than the existing interpolation-only test override.

next_steps: Restore text rendering and add a regression test proving remote error markup remains literal.
